name: Gap of Rohan
beta: From a crack behind a tree on the training wall's right side, ascend 25 feet to a stance near the Sherpa Connection tree, then continue upward beyond another tree, then via the evident break at the main wall's left. Protection up to 4 inches is adequate for leading.
overview: A pleasant crack of about 25 feet leads to a stance, after which it heads directly upward beside a tree and exits via the evident gap at the left of the steep principal wall.

name: Middle Climb
beta: Start by a tree, or slightly left when the rock is damp, then go up along the leaning corner.

current.location: fronting a tree, or a little to the west if wet

name: The BattleField
beta: Start near the centre of the pristine white wall beneath a broken thin seam; work the seam to a horizontal crack beneath the first overhang, drift leftward and upward through the tiered overhangs passing a petite triangular beak, grab the bucket at the lip, and mantle onto easier ground. Take nuts, cams to 3 inches, plus a pair of small TCUs.
overview: A superb lead all the way up, with a thrilling finish through tiered overhangs.

current.location: mid-face on the pale clean wall, beneath a broken thin seam

name: The Sherpa Connection
beta: Begin by the big tree where the ramp starts on the left, and follow the prominent rightward-angling crack all the way up; nuts plus cams from small to medium suffice.

current.location: beginning by the biggest tree at the ramp's west tip, then the crack that trends rightward

name: Unknown Quantity
beta: Begin under an aged sleeve bolt, boulder up to the layback crack, and follow it.
overview: A worthwhile route whose only hard move comes right at the start, followed by a pleasant layback crack.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: begins beneath a rusty sleeve bolt; a single bouldery pull reaches a layback crack

name: Fool on a Hill
beta:
Start at the roof sitting about face-high beside the big dihedral, gain the ledge above it by going in from the left, then follow cracks angling leftward before trending right to bolt one; delicate edging carries you by bolt two to a good layback hold.

Step onto a slim shelf and shuffle rightward to a lowering anchor that can't be seen from below; if toproping, slot a nut in to the anchor's left so the follower is spared a swing.
overview: Superb face climbing that counts among the best on the crag. Left-leaning cracks lead up to bolt one, and thin edging beyond bolt two reaches a lieback hold. A slim ledge, then a rightward traverse, arrives at the lowering anchor.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: beside the big dihedral on its right, under a head-high roof

name: Green Route
beta: Starts from the top of the bouldering wall, with an exposed sidestep at Topaz, then crosses the ledge toward the corner's foot, which the final pitch ascends; take large nuts plus cams from small through medium.
overview: Begins higher than the small bouldering wall and takes an airy sidestep past Topaz before crossing a ledge to the foot of a corner. The final pitch goes up that corner, which sits above the right-hand end of the ledge and is described as very pleasant at an easy grade.

name: Orange Peel Easy
beta: Go directly upward on solid holds to the roof, step leftward, surmount it, and top out at the anchor.
overview: Starts just beside the outermost orange stain on the left and works up solid holds toward a roof, finishing over it.

name: Post Road (aka Black Route)
beta: Start up a gentle flared crack toward the roof block, undercling rightward beneath the roof to the flaring offwidth that reaches a ledge, then carry on over the face or move leftward toward the chain anchor above Intertwine.
overview: A route needing varied techniques: a flared crack leads up to a large roof-block, and an undercling beneath the roof gives onto a flaring offwidth.

name: A Deal with the Devil
beta: Extend your placements with long slings, because the rope will drag badly as you go around the left side of the overhang.
overview: Rope drag is the main nuisance as the line turns the roof on its left side, so extend placements with long slings.

current.area_walk_in: The area begins just beyond a dirt and scree pile along the cliff-base trail and extends roughly 50 yards westward to the big roof.

name: Call of the Mild
beta: Go up the short dihedral to the right of its neighbor, threading a sling in a drilled hole higher up for protection, then follow the bolted subtle arete above.
overview: Goes up a short dihedral, where a sling can be threaded through a drill hole higher up, then follows a slight bolted arete.

current.location: beside Vertical Vice, on its right

name: Chinese Freedom
beta: Climb to the first pocket, then go straight up to the double-carabiner anchor in the middle of the shelf above.
overview: A steep, technical test with a hard crux low, a pair of huge pockets for jugs, and a demanding finish up to an anchor midway across the ledge.

current.area_walk_in: Go up the stairs, bear right to circle onto the rock's northern flank, passing buckthorn, sumac and oak trees, then switch back left and climb. The main trail leads to a junction near the base, where the big crack-corner called Jam and Jelly sits straight ahead behind a birch. Barnburner's crack lies near the right-hand margin of that face, which is the Winter Wall's right-hand end; the wall runs about 250 feet west to a scree pile.

name: Cosmos
beta: Descend the chimney from the belay ledge, then ascend the wall next to the easy groove, on its right. The funky basalt close to the top is where it gets hard.
overview: The start is a scramble down and right to a ledge with an eyebolt, which serves as the belay. The line then descends past the chimney and goes up the face beside the gentle groove, on its right, saving its hardest moves for odd-feeling basalt near the top.

name: Digit Damage
beta: Leave the approach gully and fight through an overhang to a finger crack, shift leftward, and take on a second crack above. It is a sustained fingers-and-forearms effort.
overview: From the access gully, passes through an overhang, then a finger crack, shifts leftward and finishes in another finger crack. Sustained and tiring.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the spur trail northward: level at first, then rising. After a small initial high point, drop down, go by a branch path, and make one last ascent; a striking view announces the upper edge of the climbing zone. Many routes start on a narrow ledge well below the rim, so carry cams for anchors there or lower a fixed rope to it; the trees on that ledge cannot be trusted.

name: Foreign Affairs
beta: Begin as for the neighboring route, then veer left toward the anchors capping Jam and Jelly; various alternative boulder-style starts exist to the left.
overview: Begins on Chinese Freedom, then bears off leftward toward the chains high on Jam and Jelly; several optional boulder-problem starts exist to the left.

name: Hateful Pleasures
beta: Begin by clipping the bolts along the roof's right edge, then switch over to placing nuts for the remainder, which is unusual for a sport area.
overview: Begins on bolts beside the right-hand end of the large roof before switching to nut placements. A mixed climb that blends fixed bolts and passive gear, which is unusual on a sport-oriented wall.

beta: It is the middle one among a trio of obvious cracks in the face and takes good gear if you place it well.

beta: Take the right part of the wall and place your gear in the small crack there.
overview: A thin-crack route on the face's right-hand portion, relying on a small crack for gear.

name: Wiessner Route
beta:
Open with an awkward crack on the right wall to a small stance, then step into the chimney itself and squeeze upward with very little gear to a comfortable ledge with fixed anchors.

Strenuous moves lead back into the chimney for the final pitch, which you follow to the top.
overview: A historic, narrow chimney on Humphrey's Ledge that rewards climbers who enjoy chimneying. It is strenuous and thinly protected, so it feels bigger than its grade suggests.

name: Barracuda
beta: Awkward, hard moves get you over the large roof and the wave feature, after which the line eases into thin, doubled left-facing corners that lead to the chains.

name: Bonsai Bulge
beta: Use a stick-clip for the first bolt. Layback and edge up the leaning face for about 25 feet to the break, then pull through the scoop to reach the lip anchors.
overview: A short, gently overhanging face climbed with liebacking and small crimp edges, leading to a break and then a scoop below the anchors.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Waimea path to the Darth Vader junction, bear right beyond the fork for the Id's monster crag, and keep ascending. It is easy to overlook at first. A second path traverses eastward out of Waimea, arriving above the crag.

name: Camber
beta: Climb the face clipping two bolts, then a tense sequence gets you to bolt three. Next, traverse leftward beyond the final bolt into a crack that reaches the top. A dirtier runout alternative goes directly upward from bolt two.
overview: Two-pitch face route with a hard layback over an overlap to a hanging stance, then an exposed finish past a big pine.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the open slabs on top of the buttress heading north to a brief path that descends onto a tapering shelf. Follow it beneath Pine Tree Eliminate then Airation until it dies out at some trees above Thin Air, then rope up and cross the sloping shelf (5.4 in places) to your route. Thin Air Face climbs offer a direct alternative.

name: Catch the Wave
beta: Reach the Great White anchors first, then keep going with non-stop liebacks and underclings along the flake that leans left, clipping four bolts before the anchor.
overview: An exposed extension above Great White: sustained laybacking and undercling moves up a flake crack that leans left.

beta: Begin off a ramp that slants left, then work a string of buckets rightward to a cramped resting stance. More good holds continue rightward, passing under the large sloping roof; bolt number five is an awkward clip.
overview: A jug-hauling classic on the Bonsai wall, following buckets up and right past a big angling roof to the anchors.

name: Chicken Delight
beta: Layback and jam the steep finger crack until a pod gives a solid hand-jam rest. Then follow the thin hand crack rightward to a bolt, stretch for an unexpected hold, and finish on easier rock.
overview: A leaning finger crack with a hand-jam rest in a pod, then a shallow crack past a bolt to easier ground.

current.area_walk_in: From the clifftop overlook head south along a trail descending a small drainage. Midway it veers left over a slab giving views toward Whitehorse Ledge, then swings north below the wall over a shaded terrace. The path finishes exposed; rope up for Upper Refuse or Book of Solemnity, and be careful when wet.

name: Concrete Jungle
beta: Pull up jugs from under the roofs, reach the largest roof and undercling out rightward. A white dike takes you up the wall above to a break; shift right a few feet and complete the climb in the open corner leading to the chains.
overview: A steep, bolted line that begins beneath roofs and blocks, hauls on big holds up to the largest roof, then follows a white dike and finishes in an open corner.

name: Espresso
beta: Go up the easy gully onto a ledge, then angle leftward over a horizontal break that takes a mid-sized or larger cam, arriving at the first bolt. The rest is steep, juggy rock that relaxes into a slab at the top.
overview: A pumpy, steep romp on big holds above a gully ledge, easing to a slab at the top.

overview: A hard classic of the crag: a pair of bolts lead into a roof system slanting leftward, one clip beyond it, then a mildly overhanging upper wall to anchors under another roof.

name: Flying Hawaiian
beta:
Begin from a pile of boulders under a tight dihedral and climb the curving crack, clipping two bolts on the way to a ledge. Work leftward along flakes on chunky rock to the dihedral's start.

Stem up the wild, strenuous dihedral, exit over the roof to the right, then swing back left into a squat leaning corner and the lip anchors.
overview: Far less difficult than appearances suggest. It goes up a curving crack and flakes to a clean dihedral, then escapes right over a roof.
